title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 31
paragraphs: Aristagoras accordingly came to Sardis and said to Artaphrenes that Naxos was an island not large in size but beautiful nonetheless and fertile in soil, and near to Ionia, and that it had much wealth and many slaves. “Send out then an expedition against this land,” he said, “and restore it to those who are now exiles from it. If you do this, first I have ready for you large sums of money—apart from the expenses of the expedition, which it is only fair that we who conduct it should supply—and next, you will gain for the king not only Naxos itself but also the islands dependent on it, Paros and Andros and the others called the Cyclades; and setting out from these, you will easily attack Euboea, an island large and wealthy, as large indeed as Cyprus, and very easy to conquer. To subdue all these a hundred ships are enough.” Artaphrenes replied: “You bring good news to the royal house, and in all these matters you counsel well, except as to the number of the ships; for instead of a hundred, two hundred shall be made ready for you by the start of spring. It is right that the king himself also should join in approving this matter.”
